questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and books of the writer Roald Dahl
Why chocolate is bad for children's health
A real chocolate maker who invents new products
How cocoa beans are grown in different countries
questions.why: Neil says they'll be meeting “a real life Willy Wonka” who invents and tastes chocolate bars.

questions.q: In the story Beth remembers, how does Charlie's luck change?
options: He finds some money in the street
He wins a ticket to visit the chocolate factory
He gets a job working for Willy Wonka in the factory
He invents his own chocolate bar
questions.why: Beth says Charlie's luck turns around when he wins a Golden Ticket to the factory.

questions.q: What is part of Helle Anttila's job at Fazer?
options: Buying cocoa beans and thinking of new products
Selling chocolate in shops around Finland
Writing children's books about sweets
Managing the company's 6,000 employees across Finland
questions.why: Beth says Helle buys the cocoa beans and comes up with ideas for new chocolate products.

questions.q: Which fact about Fazer is mentioned?
options: It was started by Roald Dahl's family
It mainly makes chocolate for the British market
It has only been making chocolate for 30 years
It is the biggest chocolate maker in Finland
questions.why: With over 6,000 employees, Fazer is described as Finland's largest chocolate maker.

questions.q: When asked if she travels the world eating chocolate, what does Helle suggest?
options: She does it every month
She finds travelling boring
She only eats chocolate made by other companies when she travels abroad
It would be lovely, but really she gets ideas from many sources
questions.why: She says “That would be a dream!” and explains she gets information from different sources.

questions.q: According to Helle, when is the right time to launch a product?
options: When customers want to buy that kind of product
As soon as the team has invented it
Only at Christmas and Easter
When other companies have stopped selling similar bars
questions.why: She asks when the right time is to launch a product, “when there is a consumer demand”.

questions.q: How does Helle feel when people buy a new product?
options: Relieved that she can finally rest
Worried that it won't sell for long
Proud of her team and very happy
Surprised, because she expected it to fail
questions.why: She says it feels great and she feels proud of her team.

questions.q: What does Helle think about products that fail?
options: They are embarrassing and best forgotten
They are as important as successes because you learn from them
They happen because customers aren't ready
They are always caused by bad advertising, not by the product itself
questions.why: She says flops are as important as successful products “because you always learn”.
